sections.heading: D — Special driving situations
sections.markdown:
## D — Special driving situations

Accuracy scope: every fact in Special driving situations uses one physical page of the registered Kansas handbook, with original wording and one complete claim per block.
All quantities and exceptions are edition-bound. The cited handbook is the evidence; no recollection or competitor text supplies authority.
Source flags: Night high-beam advice has exceptions on the next page; approximate block distance is not a legal feet conversion. Flood-depth examples, an annual injury statistic and a dog-acceleration maneuver lack complete assumptions. Animal headlight advice needs scope clarification. [A90] [A91] [A92] [A93]
Refresh disposition: legal thresholds and administrative procedures require rechecking against an issuer source when a later edition replaces this snapshot.

corpus_stability.reason: The bound Kansas handbook has one February 2022 revision label; the selected source contains no evidence of multiple annual corpus rewrites. Later legal or administrative changes require issuer rechecking.

verification_debt.claim_text: Page90 L49-50 recommends high beams whenever there is no opposing traffic and says twice the low-beam range; page91 L5-12 requires low beams when following, in heavy traffic, fog, snow or heavy rain. Do not teach the page90 statement as unconditional or the range ratio as a guarantee.

Page91 L30-34 says six inches reaches the bottom of most passenger cars with loss-of-control/stall risk and two feet of rushing water can carry most vehicles. Vehicle, current and road assumptions are not specified; retain both figures as source debt and do not infer a safe crossing depth.
Page91 L43-46 gives approximately40000 annual work-zone crash injuries without a study date or data source. Do not present it as a current annual count.

Page91 L48-53 says all temporary work-zone signs have orange backgrounds and black symbols. This blanket statement does not establish every regulatory sign's appearance; use text-supported orange work-zone cues without an all-sign guarantee.

Page92 L36 recommends flashers or a headlight signal to warn other drivers, while L38-40 warns that flashing headlights may freeze a deer in the road. The target and use of the headlight signal require clarification; hazard-flasher warning remains supported.

Page93 L6-8 directs slowing for a chasing dog and accelerating as it nears. Speed, clearance and surrounding-traffic conditions are absent; withhold a universal acceleration maneuver pending clarification.
